payload.reason: Hanja is considered an extinct language because it is no longer spoken and has evolved significantly from modern Korean, making it distinct from a mere script.

claims.text: Hanja is classified as a dead language in Korea, indicating it is no longer in active use for communication.
Hanja has evolved to have characteristics distinct from modern Korean and modern Chinese, further supporting its classification as a separate language rather than just a script.
Hanja was the main writing system in Korea until the 20th century, but it has since been replaced by Hangul, indicating its obsolescence as a living language.
